rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card with impostor table and dated predictions before data; a shared estimator (infra/shared/semantic_kappa.py, --verify) for HH307's kappa table; synthetic validation on the real event skeleton that caught two estimator traps before real data (additive DiD, bootstrap strata; amendments A1, A2); replication on 13 periods at two scales; natives NE41 (full call-scale kappa row) and NE34; estimates rows; confirm.py with NE24 frozen and dry-run (not run). Missing: holdout run (NE24 is the decisive involuntary scramble), file-level re-reads, history and kickoff rows.
rationale.faithfulness: The core claim (artifact loss costs more than memory loss) is not supported: the artifact channel carries allocation bits (0.14, 7/9 periods) but no measurable value (R2 wins), and the memory note carries neither. The context row replicates H15/H44's erasure cost on an independent estimator. Value tests rest on agent-chosen open flags and parallel trends; size about 0.1. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: A practical reading for scaffold builders: wipes cost working state (41% of the next 20 calls' commits), not orientation (89% return without help), so preserving tool outputs across resets matters more than pointing agents at repos or memory notes. The shared kappa estimator is reusable for HH307's other channels.

one_line: The artifact store tells an agent where to work after a context erasure (0.14 bits, 89% return) but adds no measurable output; the erased context carries the value (41% of output, kappa about 5 commits per 20 calls per bit).
